# Run VS Code Tunnel

Ensures the VS Code dev tunnel service is installed and running on the target machine. On each run the tool queries the VS Code CLI (`code tunnel service status`); when the service is not installed or not running, it performs a GitHub token pre-login, installs (or uninstalls-then-reinstalls) the tunnel service under the configured tunnel name, and re-checks that it is running. On success the result includes `code tunnel status` output.

## Configuration

Read from the tool entity's top-level properties:

| Key | Type | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `cli-path` | string | Overrides the VS Code CLI executable path. Defaults to the value resolved by `VsCodeCliLocator.ResolveDefaultCliPath()`. |
| `tunnel-name` | string | Overrides the tunnel name (`--name` passed to `tunnel service install`). Defaults to the current machine's short hostname. |

Authentication uses the GitHub token resolved by `Phantom.Workspaces.Llm.GitHubAuthTokenResolver` (either the app's stored token or `GITHUB_TOKEN`); it is passed to the CLI via the `VSCODE_CLI_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment variable rather than the command line.

## Usage

Wire the tool via a `tool-relationship`:

- `participants.tool` — the entity-id of this tool entity.
- `participants.schedule` — a `schedule` entity controlling how often the tunnel state is reconciled (a low-frequency schedule is fine; the tool is idempotent when the service is already running).
- `participants.target` — typically not needed; the tool operates on the local machine derived from the current execution context.

Set `paused: true` on the relationship to disable it. Install/uninstall/status operations use a 5-minute timeout; a timeout returns a failure result and the schedule retries on the next tick.
